description: Two objects and a map unify to an object type whose attributes unify those of the objects
notes: The input needs a null map whose element type is the dynamic pseudo-type (m), which the spec has no value for: the dynamic pseudo-type is a placeholder for a type that isn't known yet, so no value should have it as a collection's element type. Apart from that, the spec gives the same result. The objects unify attribute by attribute to object({a = string, b = object({})}), which is preferred over the map. go-cty can't make one map of the objects (a string and an empty object have no common type), so it ranks the given types (compareTypes in cty/convert/compare_types.go compares two objects attribute by attribute), tries the map first and then the object whose a is a string.
